clue.text: Florida's flashy, unruly sportsmen

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida

indicators.note: something unruly will not stay in order, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Showy, badly behaved athletes from Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: A fly-half is a rugby union position, the player who links forwards and backs; 'flashy' looks like a description but is the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly-halves are rugby players, so the plural names a kind of sportsman on the field.

clue.text: Running away from argument about Latin

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a fight can be a verbal argument
L is the standard abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: Someone flees a quarrel over a Latin point.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking flight is fleeing, so the noun names the act of escaping from danger.

clue.text: The old ship's on fire, losing bow and stern: aye-aye!

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of 'the'
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: a boat's bow and stern are its two ends, so only the inner letters survive

parts.note: the middle two letters of fire

explanation.surface: An old ship is burning, and a sailor answers an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' may look like a link, but it belongs with fire: on fire is the word fire with its ends lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are naval forms of acknowledgement, a sailor's respectful reply confirming an order from an officer.

clue.text: See, our way worked? Never mind

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or processed, so the letters before it are reshaped

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their method succeeded, then shrugs it off.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is spoken to cancel a previous instruction or remark, telling listeners to disregard it.

clue.text: For 'rutted', lower, coarser profanity

indicators.note: coarser means rougher, so the preceding letters are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry suggesting a cruder, lower-register substitute for a rude word.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word is commonly called by this name, since many English obscenities have just four letters.

clue.text: Where Tamworth is, in the sticks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the short form of Staffordshire, an English county containing the town of Tamworth
second meaning: walking poles or rods

explanation.surface: Tamworth is out in the countryside, far from anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sticks' is slang for remote countryside, which tempts the solver; here it simply means rods.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffs abbreviates the Midlands county name, and staffs are also long wooden poles carried for support.

clue.text: Goddess from The X Factor wearing bronze

definitions.note: Titans include female deities such as Rhea

indicators.note: the word worn sits inside the clothing, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a bronze skin colour is a tan
'it' is that indefinable star quality also called the X factor

explanation.surface: A contestant from the TV talent show sports a bronze outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The X Factor is a British TV singing contest, which pulls the solver toward a celebrity; here it means indefinable star quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans of Greek myth were the elder deities, and that group included goddesses like Rhea and Themis.

clue.text: Foxtrot, then Latin dance, saving time for another dance

indicators.note: saving here means except, so one letter is left out

parts.note: Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet
and then, so 'and' stands for then
the tango is a Latin American dance
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A ballroom programme lists a foxtrot, then a Latin number, with room for a third dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Foxtrot looks like a dance but gives a letter; the tango loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance for couples, so it is one more dance.

clue.text: Leader in Scandinavia to go with tax that's dearest

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Scandinavia
to wee is to urinate, colloquially 'to go'
to tax is to strain or test

explanation.surface: A Nordic leader's plan to bring in a tax that costs the most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To go' has its bathroom sense, and tax is a verb meaning to stretch someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearest and sweetest are both superlative terms of affection for the most loved person.

clue.text: Where rounds follow rounds?

parts.note: surface reading: a place where repeated circuits or cycles succeed one another
setter's reading: the clubhouse bar, where rounds of drinks follow a round of golf

explanation.walkthrough: The first 'rounds' are drinks bought for the group; the second are golf rounds of eighteen holes, so the bar counts as one hole more.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers name the clubhouse bar this way because they head there after completing the eighteenth hole.

clue.text: Debtor's note includes a one-time Murdoch company that's hard to credit

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgement of debt
taken as written
Sky, the British satellite broadcaster, was once controlled by Rupert Murdoch

explanation.surface: A financial tale of a media mogul's firm owing money, which seems unbelievable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Credit' suggests money in the surface, but the definition is an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses exasperated disbelief, said of something too outrageous for anyone to accept.

clue.text: Under canvas, by the sound of things, getting passionate

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver to go by how words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: camping under canvas means sleeping in tents

explanation.surface: Campers in their tent start getting amorous, judging by the noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are strong and fervent, the same deep emotional heat that passionate describes.

clue.text: Poem, when recited, evokes shrill birdcall

indicators.note: reciting is speaking aloud, so the answer is judged by its pronunciation

parts.note: a shrill call is high-pitched, and a dove's call is a coo

explanation.surface: A poem read aloud brings to mind a bird's piercing cry.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese verse form has three lines of five, seven and five syllables, a compact kind of poetry.

clue.text: Story concerning wabbit: Bugs Bunny heads off; what will hunter do?

indicators.note: off means removed, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a story can be a fib
in means on the subject of, as in 'in that matter'
taken as written

indicators.note: heads are the front letters, so only the opening letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of Bugs and Bunny

explanation.surface: A cartoon about a 'wabbit' hunted by Elmer Fudd, who lurks while Bugs escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: Wabbit is Elmer Fudd's pronunciation of rabbit in the cartoons; removing both B's leaves WAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter conceals himself and stays still until prey approaches, which is to ambush or lurk.

clue.text: Sets exam, gets confused, gives very short bursts of information

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher writes a test, gets muddled and blurts out snippets of facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' reads like a verb in the surface but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: SMS texts sent by phone are brief written communications, typically just a line or two long.

clue.text: Old invader's truncated call with horn

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the Saxons invaded Britain after the Romans left
to call someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: An ancient raider's battle cry was cut short, sounded with a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz musicians casually call any wind instrument, including the sax, a horn.

clue.text: She's describing romances with airy sounds

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so one word encircles the other

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to romance someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A woman telling of love affairs with breathy sighs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its old geometric sense of drawing a line round something.
explanation.definitionFit: Swooshes are rushing noises of air, like something moving fast past the listener.

clue.text: What fisherman might do to catch something resembling a shell

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as three words: throw out a mesh to trap fish
second meaning: a hand-held percussion instrument shaped like a pair of shells

explanation.surface: A fisherman trying to land a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits into three words, CAST A NET; the second is the single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are two concave wooden clappers, shaped like scallop shells, clicked together by flamenco dancers.

clue.text: It doesn't matter which clothes shop now, I've seen everything

parts.note: whatever means any one at all
Next is a British high-street clothing chain

explanation.surface: A shopper indifferent to which store, amazed by the fashions on show.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses astonished disbelief at something outlandish, as if nothing more surprising could follow.

clue.text: French author in drunken stupor

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A French writer found in an inebriated daze.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust wrote the novel sequence In Search of Lost Time, a landmark of French literature.

clue.text: What's remote, hurtling?

indicators.note: hurtling means rushing wildly, so the letters fly into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle: what is far away and speeding along?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the shuffled letters of 'remote' make a far-off body racing through space.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a distant space rock streaking at great speed through the sky.

clue.text: 'Gut-rot.' 'How?' 'Dodgy sprout.'

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound, so the letters before it are unreliable in order

parts.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dialogue about a stomach upset blamed on a bad Brussels sprout.
explanation.walkthrough: Gut-rot is British slang for an upset stomach or rough drink; 'sprout' looks like the vegetable but is a verb-turned-noun for new growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot growing from a plant is a natural offshoot, the same thing as a new bud.

clue.text: To create excitement in vicar, utter profanities for starters

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters, so each word gives its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of utter and profanities

explanation.surface: A vicar swearing would certainly liven up a parish meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To rev up a crowd is to stir them, a phrasal verb borrowed from accelerating an engine.

clue.text: Energy follows natural process

parts.note: pure means unadulterated, natural
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A science statement: energy comes after a natural mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' places the energy letter after the other piece. 'Process' is the kitchen verb, as in a food processor.
explanation.definitionFit: To purée food is to blend it into a smooth paste, which is what a food processor does.

clue.text: Following ousting of duke, relinquish claim to dynasty

indicators.note: ousting means expelling, so that letter is thrown out

parts.note: to hand over is to give up possession of something
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: After a duke is deposed, a pretender gives up a claim to a royal line.
explanation.walkthrough: HAND OVER loses its D. The House of Hanover ruled Britain from George I to Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover names the German royal house that provided British monarchs through the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

clue.text: Time running out — cue botox shot: that'll make this dish tastier

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
running out means leaving, so that letter departs from the rest

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Time is short, so it is time for a cosmetic injection, as if that would improve a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: CUE BOTOX loses its T and the rest is rearranged. OXO is a British brand of stock cube.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock cube is crumbled into stews and gravies to add savoury flavour to the food.

clue.text: Dines fancily, engorging Italian — so has to do these?

indicators.note: engorging means swallowing greedily, so one piece ends up inside another

parts.note: to sup is a rather formal word for to dine
IT is short for Italian, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: Someone gorges on Italian food at smart dinners, so must exercise it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bare word 'these', pointing back to what the overeater must do.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are abdominal exercises, the obvious penance for someone who has been overeating rich meals.

clue.text: Sees term restructured to become half-year course of study

indicators.note: restructured means rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A college reorganises its term so it lasts half the academic year.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities often divide the academic year into two halves, each an independent teaching period.
